settingName: Tambora 1815 and Northern Hemisphere climate aftermath 1816
settingDescription: A historically grounded visual world moving between tropical Sumbawa in 1815, upper-atmosphere process reconstructions, Europe and New England in 1816, and label-free global geography. The same hand-drawn 2D historical explainer DNA must remain stable while location, weather, scale and visual form change strongly with the narration.
recurringPlaces: Tambora and the Sanggar Peninsula on Sumbawa, shown with one consistent broad mountain silhouette and tropical coastal logic
European 1816 agricultural landscapes with muted fields, muddy roads and early-19th-century farm buildings
New England 1816 rural landscapes with visually distinct timber architecture and leafy summer vegetation
recurringProps: early-19th-century grain sheaves and field tools
grain sacks and baskets without written labels
timeWeatherLogic: Sumbawa begins warm and tropical before the eruption, shifts to ash-darkened local conditions during and after the blast; Europe and New England in 1816 use cold, wet, pale summer weather. Atmosphere diagrams remain clean and neutral rather than turning into modern corporate infographics.
continuityRules: Whenever Tambora reappears, preserve the same broad mountain and coastline identity while changing camera and distance.
Europe and New England must remain visually distinguishable through architecture and landscape rather than labels.
No modern borders, flags, scientific UI, written map labels or visible dates inside non-cover images.
The unknown 1808/1809 eruption must remain unidentified and generic; do not assign it to a named volcano.
Atmospheric aerosol visuals must stay schematic but mature, with clear physical direction and no visible explanatory text.
Do not reuse static medium character staging merely for consistency; continuity never overrides visual-interest rules.
